abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel cognitive-inspired knowledge reasoning paradigm for intelligent information systems that fundamentally reconceptualizes how symbolic reasoning and neural representation learning can be harmoniously integrated. Unlike conventional hybrid approaches that merely concatenate knowledge graphs with embedding techniques, our framework establishes a bidirectional alignment mechanism between symbolic knowledge structures and sub-symbolic neural representations through iterative ontological refinement. We formalize this paradigm using Category Theory, demonstrating how knowledge entities and their relationships can be mapped to functorial structures that preserve semantic consistency across abstraction levels. The theoretical analysis proves that this approach achieves computational tractability while maintaining the expressive power of first-order logic reasoning. Experimental validation on benchmark datasets for knowledge-based question answering and semantic search demonstrates that the proposed paradigm outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by significant margins in both accuracy and reasoning interpretability. This work contributes a foundational framework that redefines the relationship between knowledge representation and machine learning, opening new research directions for cognitive-inspired artificial intelligence in information systems.

Existing graph neural network approaches for recommendation systems suffer from the over-smoothing problem and inability to capture higher-order collaborative signals effectively. This paper presents an improved graph attention architecture with multi-granularity neighborhood aggregation for intelligent recommender systems. Our theoretical analysis reveals that the proposed hierarchical attention mechanism can adaptively balance the influence of different-order neighbors based on their semantic relevance, addressing the depth-accuracy trade-off inherent in message-passing neural networks. We introduce a novel information entropy-based regularization term that preserves node feature diversity during the aggregation process, theoretically proving its effectiveness in mitigating over-smoothing. The mathematical formulation demonstrates that our approach achieves linear computational complexity while maintaining superior expressive power compared to existing GNN variants. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets validate that the proposed method achieves substantial improvements in recommendation accuracy, particularly for long-tail item prediction. This work provides both theoretical foundations and practical algorithmic improvements for applying graph neural networks in recommender systems within the broader context of intelligent data analysis.

This paper presents MetaAgent, a novel multi-agent framework that fundamentally transforms how intelligent agents coordinate in complex information retrieval and decision support scenarios. The system introduces a hierarchical meta-cognitive architecture where specialized agents operate at different abstraction levels—strategic agents define high-level retrieval goals, tactical agents decompose queries and manage knowledge sources, while operational agents execute specific information extraction tasks. A key innovation lies in the dynamic role assignment mechanism that enables agents to adapt their behavior based on real-time performance feedback, achieving emergent coordination without explicit programming. The system incorporates a shared knowledge base with versioned ontological structures, allowing agents to build upon collective learning. Extensive evaluation in enterprise document retrieval and decision support applications demonstrates that MetaAgent achieves 47% improvement in complex query resolution compared to single-agent baselines. The architecture supports natural language interaction while maintaining explainable decision traces. This work represents a paradigm shift from isolated intelligent agents toward self-organizing agent ecosystems for knowledge management.

This paper presents HybriRec-KG, an improved hybrid recommender system that effectively combines collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and knowledge graph-enhanced semantic reasoning within a unified architecture. The system addresses the cold-start and sparsity challenges that plague traditional recommender systems through a novel knowledge graph embedding layer that provides rich side information for new users and items. The architecture implements a three-stage pipeline: first, candidate generation using efficient matrix factorization with knowledge graph regularization; second, semantic enrichment through entity linking and relationship extraction; third, precision ranking using a attention-based neural network that fuses collaborative signals with knowledge-derived features. A key contribution is the adaptive weighting module that dynamically adjusts the contribution of each signal based on data density and recommendation context. The system was deployed in a production e-commerce environment serving over 2 million users, achieving a 23% improvement in click-through rate and 18% increase in conversion rate compared to the previous production system. The design incorporates real-time learning capabilities with configurable update frequencies for different components.
